title: The Problem For France
gist: Charles Gave argues that the blowout in French government spreads is merely the visible symptom of a world in structurally rising real interest rates, which he traces to the unwinding of the Asian excess savings built up after 1997-98. Only the opening of the argument is available in this teaser.

insights.claim: The world has entered a period of structurally rising real interest rates, a view the author has been arguing for some time; the French sovereign spread blowout is presented as only the most visible symptom of this broader malady.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Treat French spread stress as a global real-rate regime signal rather than an idiosyncratic French fiscal story; duration and leveraged sovereigns are exposed elsewhere too.
insights.quote: I have been arguing for some time that the world has entered a period of structurally rising real interest rates.
insights.locator: I have been arguing for some time

insights.claim: French government bond spreads blew out sharply in the week before 6 Oct 2026, prompting Gavekal's Paris colleague Cedric Gemehl to publish a piece asking how wide French spreads can get.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: French spread widening is an active, live stress event as of early October 2026; watch the Gemehl piece for the country-specific ceiling.
insights.quote: As the spreads on French government debt blew out last Thursday
insights.locator: As the spreads on French government debt

insights.claim: The author defers to Gemehl on the France-specific drivers and claims the real story is the underlying global malady, implying that France-only fixes (budget, politics) would not resolve the repricing.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Fading French spread widening on political resolution alone may be premature if the driver is global real rates.

themes.theme: Asian excess savings and the real-rate cycle

insights.claim: The stock of excess savings accumulated by Asia after the 1997-98 crisis is the starting point of the author's story, and its accumulation drove a large decline in real interest rates worldwide.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: If falling real rates were caused by Asian excess savings, a reversal or drawdown of that savings stock implies the opposite pressure on real rates and asset valuations.
insights.quote: The accumulation of these excess savings led to a big decline in real rates all over the world.
insights.locator: The story starts with the stock

insights.claim: By implication, the structural rise in real rates is the unwinding of the post-1997 excess-savings effect, though the teaser is cut off before the mechanism is stated.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Full argument is paywalled; treat the unwind mechanism as inferred, not stated.
insights.locator: The story starts with the stock
